claims: A pied-à-terre tax is a proposed annual surcharge on luxury second homes in New York City valued at $5 million or more that are not used as a primary residence.
As of April 2026, Gov. Hochul and Mayor Mamdani are pushing this tax on non-resident owners.
Gov. Hochul and Mayor Mamdani are pushing the tax to raise ∼$500 million annually.
The tax targets non-residents who underutilize properties.
The proposed NYC tax targets residential units acting as a second home rather than a primary residence.
The proposed NYC tax particularly targets luxury condos.
The proposed NYC tax targets individuals who live outside the city.
The proposed NYC tax targets individuals who do not pay city income tax.
The proposed NYC tax targets owners of high-value properties.
Only properties worth $5 million or more are subject to the proposed NYC tax.
Proposals indicate a potential sliding scale for tax rates.
Proposals indicate a tax starting around 0.5% on the value over $5 million.
The purpose of the proposal is to fill city budget gaps.
The purpose of the proposal is to ensure owners of vacant high-value homes contribute to city services.
The proposal has faced opposition from the real estate industry.
The proposal has been debated for several years.
